scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified read returns the current Company's channel rows and listing rows used by the retained Ecommerce workspace catalog. The qualified commands create one draft channel and perform the retained channel activate/reject/retire and listing publish/reject/retire review transitions. Listing create, carts, checkout, Sales order handoff, Inventory reservation, Finance posting, fulfillment, returns, attachments, purchase controls and the retained command client are not claimed.
scope.domain: Ecommerce actor policy (commerce.read for the catalog, commerce.sales for writes, commerce.approve plus a Company-only assignment for review, the exact ecommerce module and selected-context expiry), Company-scoped channel/listing rows, exact channel/listing source column shapes, bounded 500-row collections with strict descending updated_at/id order, unique ids and listing channel/product pairs, currency/status/version/timestamp/config validation, trimmed 2..160 channel names, web/marketplace/social channel types, 3..2000 review reasons, kind-specific transitions, exact expected-version status/version requirements and creator independence for activate/publish/reject while allowing creator retirement.
scope.application: One storefront_catalog read requires the current actor before any repository call, reads only Company-scoped Ecommerce rows and validates every channel/listing and the descending page before presentation. create_channel resolves the canonical receipt first, inserts one draft channel, writes the idempotency receipt, audit and outbox in the same unit and validates persisted readback. review_ecommerce_record requires commerce.sales plus commerce.approve and a Company assignment, locks the owner row FOR UPDATE, validates the current status/version and creator independence, applies the exact expected-version CAS, writes the receipt, audit and outbox and validates persisted readback.
scope.adapters: Read/write SQL is Ecommerce-owned only: ecommerce_channels and ecommerce_listings, plus the existing shared command_receipts, audit_events and outbox_events written by the retained workflow command boundary. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required and no commit occurs in the adapter. No product, customer, warehouse, Sales order, Inventory, Finance or Commercial row is read or written; no cross-owner SQL is invented.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/ecommerce/catalog, POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/ecommerce/channels and POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/ecommerce/reviews. Exact Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS origin validation, empty-query rejection, application/json, Idempotency-Key, an 8 KiB body, exact catalog/channel/review input shapes, private/no-store, no-referrer and nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch scope, purchase admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_ECOMMERCE_CATALOG_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/5432/5433/5435/8080 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact channel/listing/context shapes, Company scope, unique ids and channel/product pairs, strict order, status/currency/config/version/timestamp validation and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained read.
scope.ssr: The Ecommerce workplace screen retains ecommerceWorkspace for carts, checkouts, purchase controls, products, parties and warehouses, then uses the native catalog for the channel catalog and listing cards when ERPX_NATIVE_ECOMMERCE_CATALOG_CONFIG is present. An unset configuration retains the existing workspace lists; once configured, an invalid or failed native read is surfaced through pageError rather than silently replaced.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The retained ecommerceWorkspace read remains the page's purchase-admission preflight and the composition backend must repeat current IAM, Holding/Company scope and package admission inside its own serializable read. The native read itself has no Commercial entitlement port yet; this is a composition responsibility and an explicit open item. Native channel create/review require commerce.sales, commerce.approve, the ecommerce module and a live Company assignment; composition must repeat current authority and package admission.
